source_corrections.printed_form: The direct isomorphism clause excludes q=r only.
source_corrections.evidence: Authority physical page 70 prints only q unequal to r, but physical page 71 separately defines E^(r+1) as Coker(alpha-dual), and the five-term sequence identifies that cokernel with GrExt^(r+1). T^(r-q) is also undefined there under the no. 70 convention.
source_corrections.integration: State the direct formula for 0 <= q < r, state q=r and q=r+1 through the five-term sequence, and state vanishing above r+1 separately.

source_corrections.printed_form: Each L_p is free after displaying L_p, L_(p-1), ..., L_0.

source_corrections.integration: Preserve the printed L_p in provenance and use the quantified index L_i in the corrected definition and Stacks history.

source_corrections.printed_form: The general formula uses (-1)^j for j=1,...,q, while the immediately following degree-one formula says d(e<i>)=f_i.
source_corrections.evidence: Substituting q=1 in the printed general formula gives -f_i, contradicting the next displayed line on printed p. 269. Both marks are clear at 1100 dpi-equivalent inspection.
source_corrections.integration: Preserve both printed forms in provenance and use the standard Koszul sign (-1)^(j+1), which agrees with the explicit degree-one formula. Record that the uniformly opposite convention is chain-isomorphic by multiplication by (-1)^q in homological degree q.

source_corrections.printed_form: The degree of e_(i_1...i_q) is m_1+...+m_q, independent of the selected tuple.
source_corrections.evidence: Authority printed p. 273 visibly prints sum_(j=1)^q m_j, while the basis index, differential, and following Hom-degree calculation all depend on i_1,...,i_q.
source_corrections.integration: Use m_(i_1)+...+m_(i_q), preserve the printed form in history, and retain the full external correction namespace separately.

source_corrections.printed_form: The one-based general formula again uses (-1)^j, while the same paragraph states d(e_i)=P_i.
source_corrections.evidence: At q=1 the general formula gives -P_i and the explicit clause gives +P_i. Both are clear on authority printed p. 273.
source_corrections.integration: Use (-1)^(j+1), preserve both forms, record the opposite-sign chain isomorphism, and identify this occurrence as a fresh correction linked to the global no. 75 decision.

source_corrections.printed_form: En appliquant le foncteur A à cette suite, obtient une suite exacte de faisceaux.
source_corrections.evidence: Authority printed p. 275 clearly omits the impersonal subject on. The participial clause and the exact-sheaf consequence require on obtient; the external French correction ledger independently records the same print defect.
source_corrections.integration: Preserve the omission in diplomatic provenance, restore on in corrected French, and disclose the grammatically required reading in English. No mathematical formula changes.

stacks_corrections.label: section-refinements-cech
stacks_corrections.evidence: FAC printed p. 214 and the calculation following equation-transformation
stacks_corrections.correction: gamma-prime minus gamma equals d h plus h d

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-cech-Hausdorff-quasi-compact
stacks_corrections.evidence: The baseline top Cech-complex row repeated F while the declared short exact sequence and aligned injective resolutions use F, G, H; FAC printed pp. 216--217 independently shows the three coefficients.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace the second and third top-row coefficients by G and H.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-cech-paracompact
stacks_corrections.evidence: The baseline proof chooses a boundary class and representative with coefficients in G although the lifting construction requires the quotient sheaf H; FAC printed p. 218 confirms the H-to-F boundary.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace G by H for the boundary class and its covering representative.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-cech-paracompact
stacks_corrections.evidence: The baseline proof constructs d(g) in degree n+1 but sends its colimit class to degree n; FAC printed p. 218 confirms the degree shift.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace the target by Cech H^(n+1)(X,F).

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-cech-paracompact
stacks_corrections.evidence: The baseline proof cites only the degree-one comparison while asserting both degree-zero and degree-one base cases.
stacks_corrections.correction: Cite the separately labelled degree-zero and degree-one comparison lemmas.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-when-invertible
stacks_corrections.evidence: FAC no. 58 exposes the negative-integer case: before this checkpoint the proof called multiplication by f^n a map on S and M for every integer n, although f^n belongs to the original ring only for nonnegative n.
stacks_corrections.correction: Invert f first, then use multiplication by f^n on S_f and M_f before taking degree-zero parts.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h1-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: The proof has reduced to X=P^n but chose a linear form in H^0(P^1,O(1)).
stacks_corrections.correction: Choose the linear form in H^0(P^n,O(1)).

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h1-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: For m'<m the two downward multiplication maps from twist m' to twist m require the nonnegative exponent m-m', not m'-m.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace both vertical exponents by m-m'.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h1-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: After setting y=i(x), the pushforward stalk is an O_(P^n,y)-module, while the prior proof subscripted the ambient local ring by x.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace the ambient local-ring subscript x by y.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-d-uple
stacks_corrections.evidence: The final parenthetical cross-reference in the statement lacked its closing parenthesis.
stacks_corrections.correction: Close '(see proof for precise statements)' before the lemma ends.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-d-uple
stacks_corrections.evidence: The inverse-prime proof tested a power in p-prime but concluded that g+h belonged to p-prime even though g+h lies in S.
stacks_corrections.correction: Derive (g+h)^d in p-prime and then g+h in p, and write the complete homogeneous ideal and primeness checks.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-d-uple
stacks_corrections.evidence: For S=K[x], d=2, M=S(1), and N=S(-1), the asserted tensor identity gives nonisomorphic shifts.
stacks_corrections.correction: Use the natural map beta and prove the required sheaf multiplication compatibility after localization on standard opens.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h0-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: After restricting and trivializing L on the integral closed subscheme Z, the proof switched global sections and asymptotic Riemann--Roch to X.
stacks_corrections.correction: Keep L restricted to Z, take Gamma on Z, and apply asymptotic Riemann--Roch to Z.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h0-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: The proof wrote powers indexed by deg(s) although s is a section of a negative tensor power.
stacks_corrections.correction: Write s in Gamma(Z,L^(-a)) and t in Gamma(Z,L^b) with a,b>0, then use s^(tensor b) tensor t^(tensor a).

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-vanishin-h0-negative
stacks_corrections.evidence: The proof said 'there is nothing the show' in the closed-point case.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace 'the' by 'to'.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-regular-immersion-ext
stacks_corrections.evidence: The minimal-generator function had codomain {1,2,3,...}, excluding the zero ideal and identity closed immersion.
stacks_corrections.correction: Allow nonnegative rank by changing the codomain to {0,1,2,...} and record the empty Koszul sequence case.

stacks_corrections.label: lemma-regular-immersion-ext
stacks_corrections.evidence: The final parenthetical display used RSheafHom over O_X with O_Y as its second argument, unlike the statement and proof.
stacks_corrections.correction: Use RSheafHom over O_Y in the final display.

stacks_corrections.label: spaces-over-fields-definition-euler-characteristic
stacks_corrections.evidence: The definition at tag 0DN1 read 'proper algebraic over k', while the section heading and tag 0DN2 immediately below both use 'proper algebraic space'.
stacks_corrections.correction: Restore the missing word 'space' in the definition hypothesis.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-m-regular-globally-generated
stacks_corrections.evidence: The proof's multiplication map uses degree d-m polynomials and concludes generation of F(m), so its basis vectors must lie in H^0(P^n,F(m)), not H^0(P^n,F).
stacks_corrections.correction: Choose the basis in H^0(P^n,F(m)) and record the degree-consistency repair in history.

stacks_corrections.label: coherent-lemma-cohomology-projective-space-over-ring
stacks_corrections.evidence: For d<=-n-1 the reciprocal monomial module has positive rank binom(-d-1,n); the former expression put negative d in the lower binomial index.
stacks_corrections.correction: Use binom(-d-1,n)=(-1)^n binom(d+n,n) and explain the generalized-binomial Euler identity.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-chi-tensor-finite
stacks_corrections.evidence: The zero coherent sheaf has empty scheme-theoretic support, so its support has dimension at most zero rather than dimension zero.
stacks_corrections.correction: Say the scheme-theoretic support has dimension at most zero before applying the affine zero-dimensional argument.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-exact-sequence-induction
stacks_corrections.evidence: Annihilation by the hyperplane ideal produces a sheaf on H but does not by itself identify it with i^*F as the statement requires.
stacks_corrections.correction: Use right exactness of pullback under the closed-immersion equivalence to identify the cokernel with i_*i^*F.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-hilbert-polynomial
stacks_corrections.evidence: At n=0 the zero sheaf gives the zero function, so calling every constant function degree zero overstates the required bound.
stacks_corrections.correction: Say the constant function is a polynomial of degree at most zero.

stacks_corrections.label: algebra-lemma-one-equation-module
stacks_corrections.evidence: The statement began with the phrase Let R is a Noetherian local ring.
stacks_corrections.correction: Replace is by be and retain the unchanged mathematical hypothesis.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler;spaces-over-fields-lemma-numerical-polynomial-from-euler
stacks_corrections.evidence: Both proofs began induction at support dimension zero, leaving the empty support of the zero sheaf untreated.
stacks_corrections.correction: State the Euler map is zero for the zero sheaf and begin the dimension induction only after assuming the sheaf is nonzero.

stacks_corrections.label: varieties-lemma-numerical-polynomial-leading-term;spaces-over-fields-lemma-numerical-polynomial-leading-term
stacks_corrections.evidence: For the zero sheaf d=dim(empty) is minus infinity, so the displayed strict ordinary polynomial-degree comparison is not meaningful.
stacks_corrections.correction: Separate the zero Euler map and introduce d, top-dimensional components, and the strict degree bound only in the nonzero branch.

stacks_corrections.label: algebraization-proposition-hilbert-triple
stacks_corrections.evidence: When F=0 but F_0 is a nonzero finite-length module, the proof gives a nonzero constant function although dim Supp(F) is minus infinity.
stacks_corrections.correction: State the zero-F function is constant and apply the support-dimension degree bound only when F is nonzero.
